LOSS OF LIFE FOLLOWING MAN OVERBOARD FROM P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST
Findings of Fact:
1. P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST (O.N. 1033572) is an inspected passenger vessel. The regulations
that govern P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST are found in Title 46 Code of Federal Regulations,

lines.text: Subchapter K – Small Passenger Vessels Carrying More Than 150 Passengers Or With Overnight
Accommodations For More Than 49 Passengers. P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST's last In-Service
Inspection was conducted on 13APR12. Attending inspectors issued the vessel's Certificate of
Inspection. The P/V QUEEN OF THE WEST was operated by American Cruise Lines, Inc.
Captain
was the master of the vessel at the time of the incident.
2. At approximately 1200 hrs on 06AUG12 the vessel moored at the marina in Rainier, OR, for an
overnight stay. The vessel's position was 46-05.475N 122-56.886W. Weather conditions were
observations and historical information provided by

National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) website. On scene weather was
clear with 8 nautical miles of visibility. The air temperature was approximately 62 degrees and
the water temperature was approximately 69 degrees. Winds were 6 knots from WSW. The
downstream currents were moving at approximately 4 knots. Tides were nearing the end of an
ebb cycle and the tidal height was +2.00 feet above mean low low water (MLLW).
3. At 2140 hrs Mr. Staples signed off the vessel after working an entire shift and walked to El
Tapatio Mexican Restaurant in Rainier, OR, where he purchased and drank two mixed drinks at
the bar using cash. He took a photo of his drink and posted it to his Facebook page. When he
consumed alcohol, Mr. Staples violated American Cruise Lines Operations Manual policy 3.3
(Alcohol Abuse / Alcoholic Beverages) which stated, "No member of the crew shall consume any
alcoholic beverage while on board or ashore 12 hours before performing any duty, while they are
in employ of American Cruise Lines and assigned to a vessel. Consuming any alcohol 12 hours
before any duty is prohibited."
4. At 2201 hrs he arrived at Ol' Pastime Tavern in Rainier and consumed one bottle of beer that was
purchased for him by another patron. He departed sometime around 2245 hrs.
5. Mr. Staples signed back in to the vessel at 2246 hrs and joined other members of the crew in the
dining room area to play video games until 0105 hrs. Some witnesses stated that he appeared
intoxicated and slurred his speech. Mr. Staples and other members of the crew violated American
Cruise Lines Operations Manual policy 3.6 (Crew Areas) which stated, "In no case will the crew
be able to congregate in or use the dining room after 12 midnight."Additionally, Mr. Staples and
other members of the crew violated American Cruise Lines Operations Manual policy 3.6 (Crew
Areas) which stated, “All crew members, except those on duty, are to be in their quarters after 12
midnight."

6. At 0105 hrs on 07AUG12, Mr. Staples, two deckhands (Mr.
and the other galley steward (Mr.
went out to the paddlewheel on
the port side to smoke. By doing so, Mr. Staples and other members of the crew violated Captain
standing order to not congregate on the stern of the vessel. However, there were no
written policies onboard (or from the company) that prohibit such loitering on the stern. When
questioned, witnesses were conflicted as to the policy: Some thought they could be on the stern
to smoke, others knew it was against policy.
7. At approximately 0105 hrs witnesses stated that Mr. Staples said that he was going "to take a
piss" and approached the paddlewheel between the diagonal paddlewheel post and the ftermost
bulkhead of the vessel. He was observed to stumble twice and attempt to grab the paddlewheel to
steady himself.
